request.spec:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. After that run I only edited comments, so I didn't run it again.

**Server**
- **Only drafts can be edited.** `ApplyClaim.java` now refuses an edit of any claim that isn't a DRAFT with a 400. That covers OPEN as asked, and also SETTLED and VOID, since the request says only a draft can be edited.
- **No race with a status change.** `ClaimRepository.update` now only writes while the claim is still a DRAFT, and `SaveClaim` refuses the edit if nothing was written. So an edit can't slip through if another user opens the claim at the same moment, and a refused edit writes nothing to the store or the audit file.
- **Voided claims keep their number.** `ApplyClaimStatus` no longer clears the number on void, and CLAIM_VOIDED already ends with `number=<n>` when there is one. A draft has no number, so voiding one still writes no number. The sheet's counter means numbers are still never reused.

**Front end** (`claims.slot.tsx`)
- Pressing Edit on a claim that isn't a draft shows the claim's `claim-error` ("Only a draft claim can be edited; void it and add a new one instead.") and doesn't open the editor. The error goes away on the next Edit or action on that claim.
- If another user opened the claim after the page loaded, the server refuses the save and the form's `claim-form-error` shows. I added the draft rule to that message.

I updated the comments that still said voiding clears the number (`Claim.java`, `ClaimNumber.java`, `RecordClaimStatusChanged.java`, `status.PUT.yml`). I didn't add a database migration because the schema doesn't change. Claims voided before this change already had their number cleared, and it can't be recovered, so they stay without one.
